subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw standardize a markdown per-skill preference sidecar, use structured `skills.entries.*.config`, or keep this as an unsupported user/ClawHub convention?
rationale: The feature changes the public skill loading and prompt contract, including precedence, context injection, snapshot invalidation, and config policy, so code cannot safely choose the permanent shape on its own.

options.title: Standardize markdown sidecars
options.body: Adopt a canonical `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` file, load it with the selected skill, and include it in watcher/version/docs/tests.

options.title: Use structured skill config
options.body: Route per-skill user preferences through the existing `skills.entries.<key>.config` shape and document how skill authors read it.

options.title: Keep it outside core
options.body: Decline a core loader contract for now and document user-authored skill conventions or ClawHub bundle patterns instead.

recommendation.title: Standardize markdown sidecars
recommendation.body: Adopt a canonical `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` file, load it with the selected skill, and include it in watcher/version/docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across skills docs/config/loading and is the best available routing owner for the product/API decision.
